stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Find \( \lim_{x \to 4} \left(4 g(x) - 5\right) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is -13, because g is differentiable at \( x = 4 \), so it is continuous there, and \( \lim_{x \to 4} g(x) = g(4) = -2 \).

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable at \( x = 4 \), so it is continuous there.
By the limit laws the limit is 4(-2) - 5 = -13.
worked_solution.rule_named: sum and constant multiple limit laws

options.label: The limit is -13, because the table gives a value of g at every listed input, so g is continuous at \( x = 4 \), and \( \lim_{x \to 4} g(x) = g(4) = -2 \).
options.derivation: continuity asserted on a false basis, having tabulated values, instead of on the differentiability the stem supplies
